_comment: credential-root-grants.v1.json — one ROOT GRANT per provider that offers a non-interactive mint API (Joe's ruling 2026-10-12, decision cbe91287-10a2-48d0-bda7-3b1784b4bb93: credential minting must not require him). Joe places each root grant ONCE with its one_time_command; from then on ops/credential-mint.py (nightly step 'credential mint') mints, verifies, installs, stores and revokes every child named under `children`, rotating each `rotate_within_days` before its ttl runs out. A credential this file cannot mint is marked `holder_only` with its reason in ops/config/credential-inventory.v1.json; the inventory and this file are checked against each other by lib/credential_mint.load_plan(). NEVER put a secret VALUE here. Every endpoint below is the provider's documented control-plane API; none was called while this file was written (no live provider call from a build seat), so the first night after a grant is placed is the first live exercise, and verify-before-store keeps the existing credential in place if any call is refused.

grants.name: cloudflare
grants.scope: A Cloudflare USER API token (My Profile > API Tokens > Create Custom Token) carrying exactly one permission, User > API Tokens > Edit ('API Tokens Write'), created with a 90-day TTL so Cloudflare itself ends it if it is never replaced. Children are minted under /user/tokens, so they are user-owned and the existing /user/tokens/verify probes keep working unchanged.
grants.reach: EQUIVALENT TO JOE'S WHOLE CLOUDFLARE USER. 'API Tokens Edit' lets its holder mint a new token carrying ANY permission Joe's user holds, on any account or zone he can reach: Workers deploys, DNS, R2 (where the backups live), billing and account settings. The one-permission scope limits what the token does directly, not what it can grant itself. Revoke it in the Cloudflare dashboard (My Profile > API Tokens).
grants.verify: GET https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/user/tokens/verify with the token as Bearer; HTTP 200 and result.status == 'active'. Read-only.

params._note: account_id is the CARR account mcp-server/wrangler.toml deploys to. Each child is scoped to that account only, with the two permission groups the hand-made deploy token carried (Workers Scripts:Edit + Account Settings:Read); group names are resolved to ids at mint time from GET /user/tokens/permission_groups, and an unresolvable name refuses the mint.

grants.name: neon
grants.scope: A Neon ORGANIZATION API key for org org-dry-dew-75906281 (Organization settings > API keys, created by an org admin). It is not tied to Joe's personal account.
grants.reach: ADMIN OVER THE WHOLE NEON ORGANIZATION org-dry-dew-75906281. Neon documents organization API keys as admin-level access to every organization resource: it can create, read and DELETE any project, including steep-field-48688294 (production), plus its branches, roles and databases, and it can create and revoke the organization's API keys. Revoke it in the Neon console (Organization settings > API keys).
grants.verify: GET https://console.neon.tech/api/v2/projects?org_id=org-dry-dew-75906281 with the key as Bearer; any 2xx. Read-only. The same question tools/rotate-credential.py and the neon-api-key health probe ask.

params._note: The organization tools/db-tap.py and tools/rotate-credential.py pin. Children are organization API keys (POST /organizations/{org_id}/api_keys, with project_id in the body when child_scope.kind is 'project'), revoked by id (DELETE /organizations/{org_id}/api_keys/{key_id}). lib/credential_mint.load_plan refuses a Neon grant whose child_scope is absent, or org-wide without a recorded `because`.

child_scope.because: NEON_API_KEY is one name read by consumers that span the whole organization, not one project: tools/staging-project-replacement.py creates the replacement staging project (`neonctl projects create`), tools/db-tap.py, tools/staging-fixtures.py, tools/provision-staging-app-writer.py and tools/provision-calendar-prebrief-joe.py resolve the staging project by name across the org (`projects list --org-id`), tools/system_costs.py reads org-level consumption_history, and tools/restore-watermark.py reads the production project. A project-scoped key (member access to one project) cannot serve the staging and production projects and the org reads at once, so the child is an org-wide key: the same admin reach as the root, and no wider than the hand-placed personal key it replaces. Narrowing it means splitting NEON_API_KEY by project first; then set kind 'project' with that project_id here.

grants.name: openai
grants.scope: An OpenAI ORGANIZATION ADMIN key (platform.openai.com > Organization settings > Admin keys). tools/system_costs.py already reads billing with this same name, so one placed key serves both.
grants.reach: ADMIN OVER THE WHOLE OPENAI ORGANIZATION: it can create and delete projects, service accounts and their API keys, invite and remove members, and read usage and billing. Every key it mints is metered API billing. Revoke it in the OpenAI console (Organization settings > Admin keys).
grants.verify: GET https://api.openai.com/v1/organization/projects?limit=1 with the admin key as Bearer; HTTP 200. Children are verified with GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models; HTTP 200. Read-only.

params._note: Children are service accounts of the project named here (POST /v1/organization/projects/{project_id}/service_accounts), found by name and created once if absent, revoked by deleting the service account. A minted key is installed into Codex with `codex login --with-api-key` (value on stdin, never argv), which moves Codex from ChatGPT-subscription auth to METERED API-key auth on that machine. That billing change needs Joe's explicit yes: until codex_api_billing_approved is set true here (by a PR Joe approves), the lane mints no Codex child at all and the OpenAI grant's loop says what it is waiting on.

grants.name: xai
grants.scope: An xAI MANAGEMENT API key (console.x.ai > Settings > Management keys), which can create and delete the team's API keys.
grants.reach: Would be admin over the xAI team's API keys. Not asked for (deferred).
grants.deferred: Nothing in the inventory consumes an xAI API key: Grok runs through the Grok CLI on a grok.com OAuth login (grok-cli-auth, holder_only, `grok login` offers only --oauth and --device-auth). Placing a management key today would mint children nobody reads, so it is not asked for. The first API consumer adds a child here, a store_name in lib/token_store.py, and an adapter in lib/credential_mint.py.

grants.name: github-app
grants.scope: The CARR GitHub App private key (app 5199739, installed on jbookout/carr-system), at ~/.config/carr/<key_file from ops/config/github-app.json>.
grants.reach: Installation tokens for the CARR GitHub App on jbookout/carr-system, with exactly the app's granted permissions. Unchanged by this file: already self-minting.
grants.system_command: lib/github_app_token.gh_env() — already derives a fresh installation token for every background gh call
grants.verify: Presence of the key file only (os.path.exists, never opened by the mint path). lib/github_app_token.py proves it on use: a JWT exchange for an installation token.
